name: Missional Explorations
summary: Seed funding from the Church Planting Taskforce for local outreach that could one day grow into a church plant.

body.heading: A stepping-stone to church planting
paragraphs: Missional Explorations are designed to identify local missional contexts that might one day become future church plants. They are a stepping-stone between a congregation's regular outreach and something that might take on a life of its own.
Under the supervision of the local church, a Missional Exploration might develop its own identity and, as a new congregation, lead to a formal church plant.

image.alt: Volunteers sorting boxes of donated food outside a brick church building
image.caption: A food relief drive run by a local Reformed church

body.heading: Why we fund them
paragraphs: The overall goal is to see the gospel proclaimed and the kingdom extended. Church planting is a big step, often seen as a “bridge too far”, and Missional Explorations stand in the gap between regular outreach and planting something new.
Whether or not a church plant results, we are confident that the gospel will be proclaimed, real communities will be reached and the Kingdom of God will be built up.

body.heading: Funding
paragraphs: The Church Planting Taskforce (CPT) provides seed funding in partnership with local churches. It will match the local church's contribution up to $2,500.

body.heading: Who can apply
paragraphs: If you have found a missional opportunity that could grow into a church plant with the right training and financial support, please consider applying. Groups might meet around a sporting club, a playgroup, a school community or any other setting where Christians are involved.

The application asks for a description of the initiative and its leadership team, its plans, a detailed budget and who will report progress to the CPT. The CPT is happy to help churches with their application and may ask for more information before approving it.
